content: {"claims":[{"beatId":"b1","source":"narration","text":"Why does one word get three token counts?","verdict":"no_claim","ids":[]},{"beatId":"b1","source":"narration","text":"Plain Paris, spaced Paris, shouted Paris.","verdict":"no_claim","ids":[]},{"beatId":"b1","source":"narration","text":"A token is a chunk that becomes one number.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-1"]},{"beatId":"b2","source":"narration","text":"A tokenizer turns text into tokens.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-1"]},{"beatId":"b2","source":"narration","text":"Characters keep the vocabulary — the fixed list of pieces — tiny, but paragraphs become thousands of steps.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-4"]},{"beatId":"b2","source":"narration","text":"Whole words leave new names no entry, so subword pieces sit between.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-5","fact-6"]},{"beatId":"b3","source":"narration","text":"Learning starts from raw bytes: two hundred fifty-six values, so any text can be written.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-7","num-2"]},{"beatId":"b3","source":"narration","text":"Then count neighbouring pairs, join the most frequent — 't' plus 'h' becomes 'th' — and repeat.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-8"]},{"beatId":"b3","source":"label","elementId":"byte-vocab","text":"256","verdict":"supported","ids":["num-2"]},{"beatId":"b4","source":"narration","text":"Early merges join common pairs; late merges build whole words.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-9"]},{"beatId":"b4","source":"narration","text":"Encoding replays them in that order: 'the' becomes one token, an unusual word stays in pieces.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-10"]},{"beatId":"b5","source":"narration","text":"To encode new text, pre-tokenization cuts it into chunks that merges never cross.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-15"]},{"beatId":"b5","source":"narration","text":"A space sticks to the next word; capitals break the pattern.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-15","fact-20"]},{"beatId":"b5","source":"narration","text":"So plain Paris is one token, and PARIS needs three.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-20","num-7"]},{"beatId":"b5","source":"label","elementId":"caps-count","text":"3","verdict":"supported","ids":["num-7"]},{"beatId":"b6","source":"narration","text":"Corrowby bills every request in tokens, yet the team budgeted from word counts.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-21"]},{"beatId":"b6","source":"narration","text":"English replies ran about one point three tokens per word.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-22","num-4"]},{"beatId":"b6","source":"narration","text":"A language rare in training needed about three times as many.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-23","num-5"]},{"beatId":"b6","source":"label","elementId":"stat-1-3","text":"about 1.3","verdict":"supported","ids":["num-4"]},{"beatId":"b6","source":"label","elementId":"rare-card","text":"about 3× the tokens","verdict":"supported","ids":["num-5"]},{"beatId":"b7","source":"narration","text":"So Corrowby counts tokens with the exact tokenizer of the model it calls, and writes budgets in tokens per language.","verdict":"supported","ids":["fact-26"]},{"beatId":"b7","source":"narration","text":"That reply with Paris now fits.","verdict":"issue","ids":[]}],"issues":[{"beatId":"b7","category":"unsupported_claim","severity":"blocking","owner":"scriptwriter","fields":["narration"],"evidence":[{"kind":"narration","quote":"That reply with Paris now fits."},{"kind":"fact","id":"fact-26","quote":"After the change, Corrowby counts tokens with the exact tokenizer of the model it calls, writes prompt and reply budgets in tokens, and produces per-language cost reports."}],"problem":"The notes never state that this particular reply now fits; they only say exact token counting makes budgets match billing and limits.","fix":"Replace the sentence with a supported outcome, such as that counting exactly matches what the model is billed and limited by."}]}

{"issues":[{"beatId":"b5","category":"small_stat_card","severity":"advisory","owner":"scriptwriter","fields":["stat_cards"],"evidence":[{"kind":"stat_card","quote":"3"},{"kind":"narration","quote":"So plain Paris is one token, and PARIS needs three."}],"problem":"The stat card exists only to show the count \"3\", a small number the narration already says out loud in the same sentence.","fix":"Drop the \"3 tokens for PARIS\" stat card and let the three-slot caps grid plus the spoken \"three\" carry the payoff."},{"beatId":"b7","category":"missing_trade_off","severity":"advisory","owner":"scriptwriter","fields":["narration"],"evidence":[{"kind":"narration","quote":"writes budgets in tokens per language"},{"kind":"note","quote":"You must ship and run the exact tokenizer and build per-language reporting; the team still argues over whether to use per-language tables or count every message."}],"problem":"The resolution presents exact token counting as a pure win, while the notes say it costs shipping and running the model's tokenizer plus per-language reporting, and the team still disagrees on per-language tables versus counting every message.","fix":"Add one short clause in the closing line naming the cost, e.g. that this means running the model's own tokenizer and reporting per language."}]}
